records.context: A database already damaged by an earlier resume cannot be repaired on read — the rows are gone, and nothing in the file records what they were. It can be *rewritten* from the sources outside the database, and all three writers use ``if_exists='replace'``, so re-executing one is a full repair rather than a second generation of rows: ``convert.populate_db_from_map(db, '<converted>/conversion_map.csv')`` restores the map from the CSV that sits beside the converted images, ``align.save_coordinates`` restores the stitch coordinates, and ``foreign.run_import`` restores the imported measurements.

records.context: Most of the module decides whether skipping a field is *safe*:
records.label: spacr.resume#2
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: Most of the module decides whether skipping a field is *safe*:
records.translation: Större delen av modulen avgör om det är *säkert* att hoppa över ett fält:

records.context: **A file that exists is not a file that finished.** Older versions of ``spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`` wrote ``merged/<field>.npy`` with a bare ``np.save`` straight onto the destination path, so a crash mid-write left a short, structurally valid-looking ``.npy`` on disk. Current versions write merged arrays atomically, but files left by earlier runs can still be truncated. A resume that skips on ``os.path.exists`` would accept such a field, measure whatever bytes happened to land, and put the result in the same table as the good fields. So :func:`completed_fields_in_merged` *validates*: it parses the ``.npy`` header and checks that the file is as long as its own shape claims. Anything short is reported as rejected and re-queued, never skipped.
records.label: spacr.resume#3
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **A file that exists is not a file that finished.** Older versions of ``spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`` wrote ``merged/<field>.npy`` with a bare ``np.save`` straight onto the destination path, so a crash mid-write left a short, structurally valid-looking ``.npy`` on disk. Current versions write merged arrays atomically, but files left by earlier runs can still be truncated. A resume that skips on ``os.path.exists`` would accept such a field, measure whatever bytes happened to land, and put the result in the same table as the good fields. So :func:`completed_fields_in_merged` *validates*: it parses the ``.npy`` header and checks that the file is as long as its own shape claims. Anything short is reported as rejected and re-queued, never skipped.
records.translation: **En fil som finns är inte en fil som blev klar.** Äldre versioner av ``spacr.io._load_and_concatenate_arrays`` skrev ``merged/<field>.npy`` med ett enkelt ``np.save`` direkt till målsökvägen, så en krasch mitt i skrivningen lämnade en för kort ``.npy`` på disk som strukturellt såg giltig ut. Nuvarande versioner skriver sammanslagna arrayer atomärt, men filer från tidigare körningar kan fortfarande vara trunkerade. En återupptagning som hoppar över baserat på ``os.path.exists`` skulle acceptera ett sådant fält, mäta de byte som råkade hamna där och lägga resultatet i samma tabell som de felfria fälten. Därför *validerar* :func:`completed_fields_in_merged`: den tolkar ``.npy``-huvudet och kontrollerar att filen är så lång som dess egen form anger. Allt som är för kort rapporteras som avvisat och köas om, och hoppas aldrig över.

records.context: **The measurement workflow appends rows, so existing rows must be removed prior to continuing an interrupted run.** ``_merge_and_save_to_database`` and ``filepaths_to_database`` both call ``to_sql(..., if_exists='append')``. Measuring a field again does not replace existing rows; it *inserts additional rows*. This makes downstream per-well aggregates too large without a warning. :func:`clear_field_rows` removes old rows so repeated measurement produces one consistent result. One transaction covers every affected table, so an error leaves the database unchanged.
records.label: spacr.resume#4
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Measure appends; therefore a resume must delete first.** ``_merge_and_save_to_database`` and ``filepaths_to_database`` both use ``to_sql(..., if_exists='append')``. Re-measuring a field that already wrote some rows does not overwrite them, it *adds* to them, and every per-well aggregate downstream is then computed over inflated counts with nothing anywhere to indicate it. :func:`clear_field_rows` is the delete-before-insert that makes re-running a field idempotent, and it is the reason this module exists at all. It runs in one transaction across every table the field touched, so a failure part-way leaves the database exactly as it was.
records.translation: **Measure lägger till; därför måste en återupptagning först radera.** ``_merge_and_save_to_database`` och ``filepaths_to_database`` använder båda ``to_sql(..., if_exists='append')``. Att mäta om ett fält som redan har skrivit några rader skriver inte över dem utan *lägger till* dem, och varje aggregat per brunn nedströms beräknas då på uppblåsta antal utan att något någonstans tyder på det. :func:`clear_field_rows` är raderingen före infogning som gör det idempotent att köra om ett fält, och det är skälet till att modulen över huvud taget finns. Den körs i en enda transaktion över alla tabeller som fältet berörde, så ett fel halvvägs lämnar databasen exakt som den var.

records.context: **measurements.db is not measure's private file.** ``convert`` writes ``conversion_map`` into it, ``align`` writes ``align_coordinates``, ``foreign`` writes ``foreign_*``, ``timelapse`` writes its track table — all keyed on the same four columns as the measurements, deliberately, so that they join. Discovering "tables to clear" by their columns alone would therefore find all of them, and clearing a pending microscope field of view from each would delete the only record of which vendor file became ``plate1_A01_1``, of where each microscope image field was stitched, and of imported measurements. None of it can be recomputed from the database. The tables a resume may delete from are therefore an explicit allow-list, :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES`, checked both when the list is discovered and again per table immediately before the DELETE is prepared.
records.label: spacr.resume#5
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

Discovering "tables to clear" by their columns alone would therefore find all of them, and clearing a pending field from each would delete the only record of which vendor file became ``plate1_A01_1``, of where each tile was stitched, and of imported measurements. None of it can be recomputed from the database. The tables a resume may delete from are therefore an explicit allow-list, :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES`, checked both when the list is discovered and again per table immediately before the DELETE is prepared.
records.translation: **measurements.db är inte measures privata fil.** ``convert`` skriver ``conversion_map`` till den, ``align`` skriver ``align_coordinates``, ``foreign`` skriver ``foreign_*``, ``timelapse`` skriver sin spårtabell — alla med samma fyra nyckelkolumner som mätningarna, avsiktligt, så att de kan kopplas ihop. Att hitta "tables to clear" (tabeller att rensa) enbart utifrån kolumnerna skulle därför hitta alla, och att rensa ett väntande fält från var och en skulle radera den enda uppgiften om vilken leverantörsfil som blev ``plate1_A01_1``, om var varje ruta sammanfogades och om importerade mätningar. Inget av detta (None of it) kan beräknas på nytt från databasen. De tabeller som en återupptagning får radera från är därför en uttrycklig tillåtelselista, :data:`MEASURE_OWNED_TABLES`, som kontrolleras både när listan tas fram och igen för varje tabell omedelbart innan DELETE förbereds.

records.context: **Owned by name is not owned in fact, so ownership is decided per row.** A name allow-list answers "could measure have written this table?", and there is one case where the answer to "did it?" is no: ``foreign.run_import`` copies the imported rows into the canonical ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` table when nothing of anyone else's is there, so that a purely-imported project is readable by every spaCR tool. Those rows sit under spaCR's own metadata columns in a table on the allow-list, and a table-level rule would clear them along with the pending field.
records.label: spacr.resume#6
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context
records.source: **Owned by name is not owned in fact, so ownership is decided per row.** A name allow-list answers "could measure have written this table?", and there is one case where the answer to "did it?" is no: ``foreign.run_import`` copies the imported rows into the canonical ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` table when nothing of anyone else's is there, so that a purely-imported project is readable by every spaCR tool. Those rows sit under spaCR's own metadata columns in a table on the allow-list, and a table-level rule would clear them along with the pending field.
records.translation: **Ägd till namnet är inte ägd i praktiken, så ägarskapet avgörs per rad.** En tillåtelselista med namn besvarar frågan "kan measure ha skrivit den här tabellen?", och det finns ett fall där svaret på "gjorde den det?" är nej: ``foreign.run_import`` kopierar de importerade raderna till den kanoniska tabellen ``cell`` / ``nucleus`` / ``pathogen`` när inget som tillhör någon annan finns där, så att ett rent importerat projekt kan läsas av alla spaCR-verktyg. Dessa rader ligger under spaCR:s egna metadatakolumner i en tabell på tillåtelselistan, och en regel på tabellnivå skulle rensa dem tillsammans med det väntande fältet.

records.context: The rows are told apart by ``foreign_columns``, written by every release of the importer, names each column that importer put in each table. Its table-scoped use — ``foreign._importer_owns``, "are this table's columns a subset of what the importer recorded?" — has a row-scoped twin, and that is the rule here: **a row is the importer's when every column it is non-NULL in is one the importer recorded for this table**. A ``measure_crop`` row always carries at least its own area and intensity columns, which the importer never wrote; an imported row carries only metadata and ``foreign_``-prefixed measurements. So a table can be half one and half the other and each row is still attributable — which matters, because a project that was imported and then measured is exactly that. See :func:`measure_rows_clause`.
records.label: spacr.resume#7
records.review_basis: Direct AI technical authoring against exact current English source and normal target-neutral context

A ``measure_crop`` row always carries at least its own area and intensity columns, which the importer never wrote; an imported row carries only metadata and ``foreign_``-prefixed measurements. So a table can be half one and half the other and each row is still attributable — which matters, because a project that was imported and then measured is exactly that. records.translation: Raderna skiljs åt med ``foreign_columns``, som skrivs av varje version av importören och namnger varje kolumn som importören lade i varje tabell. Dess användning på tabellnivå — ``foreign._importer_owns``, "är tabellens kolumner en delmängd av det som importören registrerade?" — har en motsvarighet på radnivå, och det är den regel som gäller här: **en rad tillhör importören när varje kolumn där den inte är NULL är en kolumn som importören registrerade för tabellen**. En rad från ``measure_crop`` har alltid åtminstone sina egna kolumner för area och intensitet, som importören aldrig skrev; en importerad rad har bara metadata och mätningar med prefixet ``foreign_``. En tabell kan alltså vara till hälften det ena och till hälften det andra och varje rad kan ändå tillskrivas rätt ursprung — vilket spelar roll, eftersom ett projekt som först importerats och sedan mätts är just sådant. Se :func:`measure_rows_clause`.

records.context: Ownership is not read from a table-level marker such as ``foreign_import.canonical_table_written``. A marker that blocks every delete from a claimed table would also block clearing fields the import never covered, so such a project could never be resumed; and the first importer release wrote the canonical copy without that marker. ``foreign_columns`` is per table and per column, and every importer release has written it.
records.label: spacr.resume#8

records.source: Ownership is not read from a table-level marker such as ``foreign_import.canonical_table_written``. A marker that blocks every delete from a claimed table would also block clearing fields the import never covered, so such a project could never be resumed; and the first importer release wrote the canonical copy without that marker. ``foreign_columns`` is per table and per column, and every importer release has written it.
records.translation: Ägarskapet läses inte från en markör på tabellnivå som ``foreign_import.canonical_table_written``. En markör som blockerar varje radering från en tagen tabell skulle också blockera rensning av fält som importen aldrig omfattade, så ett sådant projekt skulle aldrig kunna återupptas; dessutom skrev importörens första version den kanoniska kopian utan den markören. ``foreign_columns`` finns per tabell och per kolumn, och varje version av importören har skrivit den.

records.context: **An imported copy is released before measure appends to its table.** ``measure_crop`` appends, so the moment spaCR measures a microscope field of view into a canonical table an import filled, its rows and theirs sit in the same table with nothing marking the seam and every per-microplate sample position count becomes the sum of two populations. :func:`supersede_imported_copies` executes before the first insert and removes that copy — but only when every microscope field of view it covers is either already measured into that table or queued to be measured now, and only after :func:`spacr.foreign.release_canonical_copy` has proved, row by row, that each row it removes still exists in ``foreign_<object>``. A half-released table is worse than an unreleased one, so anything less than a complete, lossless release is refused and reported instead, together with the two lines that do it by hand.

records.source: **An imported copy is released before measure appends to its table.** ``measure_crop`` appends, so the moment spaCR measures a field into a canonical table an import filled, its rows and theirs sit in the same table with nothing marking the seam and every per-well count becomes the sum of two populations. :func:`supersede_imported_copies` runs before the first insert and removes that copy — but only when every field it covers is either already measured into that table or queued to be measured now, and only after :func:`spacr.foreign.release_canonical_copy` has proved, row by row, that each row it removes still exists in ``foreign_<object>``. A half-released table is worse than an unreleased one, so anything less than a complete, lossless release is refused and reported instead, together with the two lines that do it by hand.
records.translation: **En importerad kopia frigörs innan measure lägger till i dess tabell.** ``measure_crop`` lägger till, så i samma ögonblick som spaCR mäter ett fält till en kanonisk tabell som en import har fyllt ligger dess rader och importens i samma tabell utan något som markerar skarven, och varje antal per brunn blir summan av två populationer. :func:`supersede_imported_copies` körs före den första infogningen och tar bort den kopian — men bara när varje fält som den omfattar antingen redan är mätt till den tabellen eller står i kö för att mätas nu, och bara efter att :func:`spacr.foreign.release_canonical_copy` rad för rad har visat att varje rad som tas bort fortfarande finns i ``foreign_<object>``. En halvt frigjord tabell är värre än en som inte frigjorts alls, så allt som är mindre än en fullständig och förlustfri frigöring avvisas och rapporteras i stället, tillsammans med de två rader som gör det för hand.
